item.title: My Benchmark Was 4x Wrong Because of WSL
item.description: I do most of my benchmarking on a Windows box in WSL2. It’s the machine on my desk with 32 threads and 62 GB of RAM. Everybody who does that learns the first rule early: don’t put your data on /mnt/c. DrvFs is the 9p-backed mount that exposes the Windows drives inside WSL, and it’s slow for file-heavy work. So the databases, the docroot and the build output all live on the WSL ext4 disk. My scaling harness for ePHPm even says so in capital letters in its README.
